question: Given $A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & x \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}$, find all values of $x$ such that $A$ is equal to its own inverse.
explanation:
For $A = A^{-1}$, using the formula $A^{-1} = \frac{1}{|A|}\text{adj}(A)$.

First, $|A| = (1)(1) - (0)(x) = 1$.

Adj $A = \begin{pmatrix}1 & 0 \\ -x & 1\end{pmatrix}$.

So, $A^{-1} = \begin{pmatrix}1 & 0 \\ -x & 1\end{pmatrix}$.

Equate $A = A^{-1}$:

$\Rightarrow \begin{pmatrix}1 & x \\ 0 & 1\end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix}1 & 0 \\ -x & 1\end{pmatrix}$

So, $x=0$ and $-x=0 \implies x=0$.

Thus, the only value is $x=0$.
